::: callout-note
## The 30-second version

On **German Credit** (`credit-g`, 1,000 rows, 30% bad loans) we run the full
iter8ml loop — train → calibrate → explain → monitor drift → export — in a
handful of API calls. With **default hyperparameters, CatBoost scores
ROC-AUC ≈ 0.79**, matching the [committed Phase-1 benchmark](https://github.com/minghao51/iter8ml/blob/main/benchmarks/results/credit-g_default.json)
(0.796). Optuna HPO (40 trials) edges that to **≈ 0.796**, the published
state-of-the-art band for this notoriously noisy dataset. The headline is not a
new SOTA — it is that **strong defaults + a production-ready bundle arrive in
one command**.
:::

## 1. Why this dataset

`credit-g` is a classic, recognizable credit-risk benchmark (1,000 applicants,
20 mixed numeric/categorical features, binary "good"/"bad" outcome). It is
small and noisy — published results cluster tightly around **ROC-AUC 0.79–0.80**,
and the honest finding below is that hyperparameters barely move the needle.
That makes it an ideal showcase for the thing iter8ml is actually built for:
getting a defensible, explained, exportable model onto a real dataset with
minimum ceremony.

## 2. Load & explore

```{python}
#| label: load-data
#| cache: true
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml

raw = fetch_openml(data_id=31, as_frame=True, parser="auto")
df = pl.from_pandas(raw.frame)
# Numeric risk target: 1 = bad credit (the ~30% minority, the class we care about)
df = df.with_columns((pl.col("class") == "bad").cast(pl.Int64).alias("risk")).drop("class")
TARGET = "risk"

n_bad = int(df[TARGET].sum())
print(f"shape={df.shape}  |  bad-rate={df[TARGET].mean():.1%} ({n_bad}/{len(df)})")
print(f"features: {df.width - 1}  |  types: "
      f"{sum(pl.Int64 == dt or pl.Float64 == dt for dt in df.dtypes)-1} numeric, "
      f"{sum(dt == pl.Categorical or dt == pl.Utf8 or dt == pl.String for dt in df.dtypes)} categorical")
df.head(3)
```

```{python}
#| label: class-balance
#| fig-cap: "Class balance — the 'bad credit' minority (30%) is the target class."
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3
counts = df.group_by(TARGET).len().sort(TARGET)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3))
ax.bar(["good (0)", "bad (1)"], counts["len"].to_list(), color=["#4C72B0", "#C44E52"])
for i, c in enumerate(counts["len"].to_list()):
    ax.text(i, c + 10, str(c), ha="center", fontsize=10)
ax.set_ylabel("applicants")
ax.set_title("German Credit — class balance")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 3. Baseline: the full loop with defaults

One `session.run(...)` drives the entire pipeline — preprocessing, automated
feature engineering, 5-fold CV across three GBDT families, probability
calibration, and SHAP — for free.

```{python}
#| label: baseline-run
#| cache: true
from iter8ml import ExperimentConfig, ExperimentSession, TaskType

session = ExperimentSession()
config = ExperimentConfig(
    name="german_baseline",
    task=TaskType.CLASSIFICATION,
    target_col=TARGET,
    data_path="",
    models=["catboost", "lightgbm", "xgboost"],
    cv_folds=5,
    metrics=["roc_auc", "f1_macro"],
    shap_enabled=True,
    random_seed=42,
    max_workers=1,
)
results = session.run(config, df)
for model, entry in results.items():
    if isinstance(entry, dict) and "cv_scores" in entry:
        auc = entry["cv_scores"].get("roc_auc", float("nan"))
        print(f"  {model:16s} roc_auc={auc:.4f}")
```

```{python}
#| label: leaderboard
lb = session.leaderboard().filter(pl.col("model").is_in(["CatBoost", "LightGBM", "XGBoost"]))
lb.select("model", "primary_metric", "primary_score", "duration_seconds")
```

```{python}
#| label: baseline-chart
#| fig-cap: "Baseline ROC-AUC (5-fold CV). CatBoost leads at ≈0.79 — already at the published benchmark."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.5
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
ax.barh(lb["model"].to_list()[::-1], lb["primary_score"].to_list()[::-1],
        color="#4C72B0")
ax.set_xlim(0.7, 0.82)
ax.set_xlabel("ROC-AUC (5-fold CV)")
ax.set_title("Baseline leaderboard — German Credit")
for y, v in enumerate(lb["primary_score"].to_list()[::-1]):
    ax.text(v + 0.002, y, f"{v:.4f}", va="center", fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 4. Tuning the champion (HPO)

We optimize the champion (CatBoost) with Optuna over depth, learning rate,
L2-leaf regularisation, and iterations. The data adapter returns raw columns, so
we ordinal-encode categoricals for the HPO/SHAP path — the same convention the
benchmark suite uses.

```{python}
#| label: encode-for-hpo
#| cache: true
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder

from iter8ml.data.adapter import DataAdapter
from iter8ml.engine.evaluator import Evaluator
from iter8ml.engine.hpo import optimize_model
from iter8ml.engine.models.factory import get_model_class
from iter8ml.engine.models.model_configs import ModelConfigs

adapter = DataAdapter()
X, y = adapter.transform(df, TARGET)
FEATURE_NAMES = [c for c in df.columns if c != TARGET]

# Ordinal-encode any object columns (mirrors benchmarks/openml_benchmark.py).
if X.dtype == object or (hasattr(X.dtype, "kind") and X.dtype.kind in ("U", "S", "O")):
    str_cols = [i for i in range(X.shape[1]) if X[:, i].dtype == object]
    for i in str_cols:
        try:
            X[:, i] = X[:, i].astype(float)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
    str_cols = [i for i in range(X.shape[1]) if X[:, i].dtype == object]
    if str_cols:
        enc = OrdinalEncoder(handle_unknown="use_encoded_value", unknown_value=-1)
        X[:, str_cols] = enc.fit_transform(X[:, str_cols])
    X = X.astype(np.float64)

hpo_cfg = ExperimentConfig(
    name="german_hpo", task=TaskType.CLASSIFICATION, target_col=TARGET,
    data_path="", cv_folds=5, metrics=["roc_auc"], random_seed=42,
)
evaluator = Evaluator(hpo_cfg)
search_space = ModelConfigs().catboost.hpo_search_space()
print("search space:", search_space)
```

```{python}
#| label: hpo-run
#| cache: true
hpo = optimize_model(
    get_model_class("catboost"), X, y, evaluator, "catboost",
    n_trials=40, search_space=search_space, task="classification",
)
print(f"best ROC-AUC: {hpo['best_value']:.4f}  (baseline CatBoost ≈ 0.7913)")
print("best params:")
for k, v in hpo["best_params"].items():
    print(f"  {k:14s} {v}")
```

```{python}
#| label: hpo-importance
#| fig-cap: "Hyperparameter importance (PedAnova). All values are low — on 1,000 noisy rows, the data, not the knobs, is the ceiling."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3
imp = hpo.get("param_importances") or []
if imp:
    names = [d["param"] for d in imp]
    vals = [d["importance"] for d in imp]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))
    ax.barh(names[::-1], vals[::-1], color="#55A868")
    ax.set_xlabel("importance")
    ax.set_title("HPO — what moved the needle (barely)")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
else:
    print("param importances unavailable")
```

::: callout-important
## The honest result
HPO lifts ROC-AUC by roughly **+0.005** (≈0.791 → ≈0.796). That is within
fold-to-fold variance — not a breakthrough. It confirms what the low parameter
importances show: on `credit-g`, well-chosen defaults are already near-optimal.
**The portfolio signal is that this entire loop — tuned, calibrated, explained,
drift-monitored, and exported — ran in a few API calls.**
:::

## 5. Explain the champion (SHAP)

We fit the champion on the encoded matrix and inspect global feature
attribution. The top risk drivers are exactly what a credit underwriter would
expect.

```{python}
#| label: shap-explain
#| cache: true
import shap

from iter8ml.analysis.explainability import Explainer

champion = get_model_class("catboost")(task="classification")
champion.fit(X, y)
explainer = Explainer(champion, feature_names=FEATURE_NAMES)
shap_result = explainer.explain(X[:500], run_id="german_case_study",
                                max_display=15, generate_plots=False)

print("Top features by mean |SHAP|:")
for f in shap_result.top_features[:8]:
    print(f"  {f.feature_name:26s} {f.importance:.4f}")
```

```{python}
#| label: shap-beeswarm
#| fig-cap: "SHAP beeswarm — checking_status and credit_history dominate risk attribution; each dot is one applicant."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
tree_explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(champion._model)
sv = tree_explainer(X[:500])
plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6))
shap.plots.beeswarm(sv, max_display=12, show=False)
plt.title("What drives 'bad credit' risk (German Credit)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: shap-top-bar
#| fig-cap: "Global SHAP importance — the model's risk ranking aligns with domain intuition."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
top = shap_result.top_features[:10]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
ax.barh([f.feature_name for f in top][::-1], [f.importance for f in top][::-1],
        color="#4C72B0")
ax.set_xlabel("mean |SHAP value|")
ax.set_title("Global SHAP importance (CatBoost)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 6. Monitor for drift

`credit-g` has no timestamps, so we **simulate** a production batch by holding
out half the data and injecting shift into `credit_amount` and `age`. This
matches the real `iter8 drift` interface (`--reference … --new …`) and
demonstrates detection capability honestly.

```{python}
#| label: drift-check
#| cache: true
shuffled = df.sample(fraction=1.0, seed=42)
half = len(shuffled) // 2
reference = shuffled.slice(0, half)
current = shuffled.slice(half, half).clone()
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
current = current.with_columns(
    (pl.col("credit_amount") * 1.6 + 500).alias("credit_amount"),
    (pl.col("age") + rng.normal(0, 6, current.height)).alias("age"),
)

drift = session.drift_check(
    reference.drop(TARGET), current.drop(TARGET), method="psi",
)
print(f"drift_detected: {drift.drift_detected}")
```

```{python}
#| label: drift-chart
#| fig-cap: "Per-feature PSI. The injected credit_amount shift is flagged severe; untouched features stay calm."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
rows = []
if drift.psi_report is not None:
    for fp in drift.psi_report.feature_psi:
        rows.append({"feature": fp.feature, "psi": fp.psi_value, "level": fp.drift_level})
psi_df = pl.DataFrame(rows).filter(pl.col("psi") > 0.01).sort("psi", descending=True)
if psi_df.height:
    colors = ["#C44E52" if lvl == "severe" else "#DD8452" if lvl != "none" else "#4C72B0"
              for lvl in psi_df["level"].to_list()]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
    ax.barh(psi_df["feature"].to_list()[::-1], psi_df["psi"].to_list()[::-1], color=colors[::-1])
    ax.axvline(0.25, color="gray", linestyle="--", linewidth=1, label="PSI 0.25 threshold")
    ax.set_xlabel("Population Stability Index")
    ax.set_title("Drift between reference and simulated batch")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

## 7. Promote & export the champion

Finally, promote the baseline champion and export a portable bundle.

```{python}
#| label: export
#| error: true
best_run_id = lb.row(0, named=True)["run_id"]
promo = session.promote(best_run_id, "german:classification")
print(f"promoted: {promo.selected_model} (status={promo.status})")

export_path = session.export("german:classification")
print(f"exported bundle: {export_path}")
```

## 8. Summary

| Stage | Method | ROC-AUC (5-fold CV) |
|-------|--------|--------------------:|
| Published Phase-1 benchmark | CatBoost defaults | 0.796 |
| This study — baseline loop | CatBoost defaults (full pipeline) | ≈ 0.791 |
| This study — baseline loop | LightGBM defaults | ≈ 0.769 |
| This study — baseline loop | XGBoost defaults | ≈ 0.760 |
| This study — HPO champion | CatBoost, 40 Optuna trials | ≈ 0.796 |

**Takeaways**

- **Defaults are defensible.** Out-of-the-box CatBoost lands on the published
  benchmark; no tuning required for a credible baseline.
- **HPO is honest, not heroic.** A +0.005 lift and near-zero parameter
  importance confirm `credit-g` is data-limited — the framework tells you this
  via PedAnova importances rather than hiding it.
- **Explanations are domain-aligned.** SHAP ranks `checking_status`,
  `credit_history`, and `savings_status` on top — exactly the signals a credit
  reviewer trusts.
- **Production-readiness is free.** Calibrated probabilities, drift monitoring,
  and a portable export bundle come from the same loop, not separate scripts.
